title.english: The Te-Form Helper Verbs: ている, ておく, てしまう, and More
title.japanese: て{形|けい}の{補|ほ}{助|じょ}{動|どう}{詞|し}

body:
## What Are Te-Form Helpers?

A handful of everyday verbs — ⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧, ⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧, ⟦おく→置く：01092_oku⟧, ⟦しまう→仕舞う：03064_shimau⟧, ⟦みる→見る：00283_miru⟧, ⟦いく→行く：00119_iku⟧, and ⟦くる→来る：00254_kuru⟧ — do double duty. On their own they mean "be," "put," "finish," "see," "go," and "come." Attached to the te-form of another verb, they lose most of that literal meaning and instead say **how** the action unfolds: whether it is in progress, finished, done in advance, tried out, or moving toward or away from the speaker. Japanese grammar calls them ⟦{補助動詞|ほじょどうし}→補助動詞：30818_hojodoushi⟧ (helper verbs), and they are normally written in kana.

These forms are everywhere in speech, so learning to read them quickly — and to hear their contracted forms — makes a large difference to comprehension.

## ⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧: In Progress, or in a State

〜⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ is the first helper most learners meet, and the most misunderstood. It has two main meanings, and the verb decides which one you get.

**Action in progress** — with verbs that describe an activity that lasts over time:
- ⟦{本|ほん}→本：00111_hon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}ん→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦でいる→ている：30376_teiru⟧ — I am reading a book.
- ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{待|ま}っ→待つ：00469_matsu⟧⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ — I am waiting for a friend.

**Resulting state** — with verbs that describe a change that happens in an instant. Here 〜⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ means the change has already happened and its result continues:

| Verb | 〜⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ means |
|------|--------------|
| ⟦{知|し}る→知る：00458_shiru⟧ (to come to know) | ⟦{知|し}っ→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ — I know |
| ⟦{結婚|けっこん}→結婚：02514_kekkon⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to get married) | ⟦{結婚|けっこん}→結婚：02514_kekkon⟧し⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ — is married |
| ⟦{死|し}ぬ→死ぬ：00669_shinu⟧ (to die) | ⟦{死|し}ん→死ぬ：00669_shinu⟧⟦でいる→ている：30376_teiru⟧ — is dead |
| ⟦{持|も}つ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧ (to take hold of) | ⟦{持|も}っ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ — I have (it) |
| ⟦{住|す}む→住む：00673_sumu⟧ (to take up residence) | ⟦{住|す}ん→住む：00673_sumu⟧⟦でいる→ている：30376_teiru⟧ — I live (in) |
| ⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧ (to open) | ⟦{開|あ}い→開く：00689_aku⟧⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ — is open |
| ⟦{壊|こわ}れる→壊れる：00791_kowareru⟧ (to break) | ⟦{壊|こわ}れ→壊れる：00791_kowareru⟧⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ — is broken |
| ⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧ (to go) | ⟦{行|い}っ→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ — has gone (and is there) |

The last row catches many learners: ⟦{田中|たなか}→田中：09528_tanaka⟧さん⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{東京|とうきょう}→東京：09564_toukyou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}っ→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦ています→ている：30376_teiru⟧ means Tanaka has gone to Tokyo and is there now, not that he is on his way.

A third use is **habit or repetition**: ⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧⟦{走|はし}っ→走る：00519_hashiru⟧⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ (I run every morning), ⟦{銀行|ぎんこう}→銀行：00578_ginkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{勤|つと}め→勤める：00902_tsutomeru⟧⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ (I work at a bank).

Two practical points:
- The negative of ⟦{知|し}っ→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ is ⟦{知|し}らない→知る：00458_shiru⟧, not ⟦{知|し}っ→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦ていない→ている：30376_teiru⟧.
- In casual speech the い drops: ⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦てる→てる：30816_teru⟧, ⟦{知|し}っ→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦てる→てる：30816_teru⟧, ⟦{何|なに}→何：00498_nani⟧し⟦てる→てる：30816_teru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧？ This contracted form, ⟦てる→てる：30816_teru⟧, is what you will hear in conversation and see in manga and text messages.

## ⟦てある→てある：30377_tearu⟧: Someone Did It on Purpose

〜⟦てある→てある：30377_tearu⟧ attaches to a **transitive** verb and describes a state that exists because somebody deliberately created it and left it that way. The thing affected takes ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ (or ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧), even though the verb is transitive.

- ⟦{窓|まど}→窓：02254_mado⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|あ}け→開ける：00563_akeru⟧⟦てある→てある：30377_tearu⟧ — The window has been left open (someone opened it).
- ⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{書|か}い→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦てある→てある：30377_tearu⟧ — There is a name written on it.
- ⟦ビール→ビール：01015_biiru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{冷|ひ}やし→冷やす：02403_hiyasu⟧⟦てある→てある：30377_tearu⟧ — The beer has been chilled (and is ready).

Compare ⟦{窓|まど}→窓：02254_mado⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|あ}い→開く：00689_aku⟧⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ (the window is open — a plain description) with ⟦{窓|まど}→窓：02254_mado⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|あ}け→開ける：00563_akeru⟧⟦てある→てある：30377_tearu⟧ (the window has been opened for a reason). The verb pairs behind this contrast are the subject of [Transitive and Intransitive Verb Pairs](transitive-intransitive.html).

## ⟦ておく→ておく：30378_teoku⟧: Getting Ready, or Leaving Things Be

〜⟦ておく→ておく：30378_teoku⟧ (literally "do and put") means doing something now for a later purpose:
- ⟦{切符|きっぷ}→切符：00643_kippu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}っ→買う：00489_kau⟧⟦ておく→ておく：30378_teoku⟧ — to buy the tickets in advance
- ⟦ホテル→ホテル：01027_hoteru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{予約|よやく}→予約：01522_yoyaku⟧し⟦ておいた→ておく：30378_teoku⟧ — I booked a hotel ahead of time.
- ⟦{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}→晩ご飯：02940_bangohan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}って→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧おく⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧ — I'll make dinner (so it's ready when you get back).

It also means leaving a situation as it is:
- ⟦{窓|まど}→窓：02254_mado⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}けて→開ける：00563_akeru⟧おいて⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧ — Please leave the window open.
- ⟦そのまま→そのまま：03322_sonomama⟧にし⟦ておこう→ておく：30378_teoku⟧ — Let's leave it as it is.

In speech 〜⟦ておく→ておく：30378_teoku⟧ contracts to 〜⟦とく→とく：30817_toku⟧: ⟦{買|か}っ→買う：00489_kau⟧⟦とく→とく：30817_toku⟧, ⟦やっ→やる：02980_yaru⟧⟦とく→とく：30817_toku⟧, ⟦{調|しら}べ→調べる：01213_shiraberu⟧⟦とく→とく：30817_toku⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧.

## ⟦てしまう→てしまう：03102_teshimau⟧: Finished, or Regrettably Done

〜⟦てしまう→てしまう：03102_teshimau⟧ has two flavors, and context usually makes clear which is meant.

**Completion** — the action is carried through to the end:
- ⟦{本|ほん}→本：00111_hon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{全部|ぜんぶ}→全部：02888_zenbu⟧⟦{読|よ}ん→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦でしまった→てしまう：03102_teshimau⟧ — I finished reading the whole book.
- ⟦{宿題|しゅくだい}→宿題：00812_shukudai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{先|さき}→先：02883_saki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦やっ→やる：02980_yaru⟧⟦てしまおう→てしまう：03102_teshimau⟧ — Let's get the homework out of the way first.

**Regret or accident** — something happened that the speaker did not want:
- ⟦{財布|さいふ}→財布：00663_saifu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れ→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧⟦てしまった→てしまう：03102_teshimau⟧ — I forgot my wallet.
- ⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遅|おく}れ→遅れる：00741_okureru⟧⟦てしまいました→てしまう：03102_teshimau⟧ — I ended up missing the train.

The casual contraction is 〜⟦ちゃう→ちゃう：08784_chau⟧ (from 〜⟦てしまう→てしまう：03102_teshimau⟧) and 〜じゃう (from 〜⟦でしまう→てしまう：03102_teshimau⟧): ⟦{忘|わす}れ→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧⟦ちゃった→ちゃう：08784_chau⟧, ⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦ちゃった→ちゃう：08784_chau⟧, ⟦{死|し}ん→死ぬ：00669_shinu⟧⟦じゃった→ちゃう：08784_chau⟧. Use the full form in polite and written Japanese.

## ⟦てみる→てみる：30510_temiru⟧: Give It a Try

〜⟦てみる→てみる：30510_temiru⟧ ("do and see") means doing something to find out what happens:
- ⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦てみる→てみる：30510_temiru⟧ — to try (eating) it
- ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{聞|き}い→聞く：00483_kiku⟧⟦てみます→てみる：30510_temiru⟧ — I'll ask the teacher and see.
- ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{靴|くつ}→靴：00725_kutsu⟧、⟦{履|は}いて→履く：00700_haku⟧みて⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ — May I try these shoes on?

Common patterns are 〜⟦てみたい→てみる：30510_temiru⟧ (I'd like to try...), 〜⟦てみたら→てみる：30510_temiru⟧？ (why don't you try...?), and 〜てみて⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧ (please try...).

## ⟦ていく→ていく：30814_teiku⟧ and ⟦てくる→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧: Direction in Space and Time

⟦いく→行く：00119_iku⟧ and ⟦くる→来る：00254_kuru⟧ keep their sense of movement away from or toward the speaker, but the movement can be physical or in time.

**Physical direction:**
- ⟦{傘|かさ}→傘：00639_kasa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦ていく→ていく：30814_teiku⟧ — to take an umbrella (along with you)
- ⟦{傘|かさ}→傘：00639_kasa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦てくる→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ — to bring an umbrella
- ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{連|つ}れ→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧⟦てきた→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ — I brought a friend.
- ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦{遅|おそ}く→遅い：00533_osoi⟧⟦{帰|かえ}っ→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧⟦てきた→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ — My father came home late at night.

**Go, do, and come back:** 〜⟦てくる→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ after an action means going to do it and returning: ⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}っ→買う：00489_kau⟧⟦てくる→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ (I'll go get some bread). This is the くる in ⟦{行|い}っ→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦てきます→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧, said when leaving the house.

**Change over time:** 〜⟦てくる→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ describes a change that has developed up to now; 〜⟦ていく→ていく：30814_teiku⟧ describes one that continues from now on.
- ⟦{暖|あたた}かく→暖かい：00618_atatakai⟧⟦なっ→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦てきた→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ — It has gotten warmer (recently).
- ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{分|わ}かっ→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧⟦てきた→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ — I've begun to understand Japanese.
- ⟦{人口|じんこう}→人口：01618_jinkou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{減|へ}って→減る：01985_heru⟧いくだろう — The population will keep decreasing.
- ⟦これから→これから：01287_korekara⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{勉強|べんきょう}→勉強：00770_benkyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続ける：01231_tsuzukeru⟧⟦ていきます→ていく：30814_teiku⟧ — I will keep on studying.

**Emergence:** 〜⟦てくる→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ also marks something appearing or starting: ⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{降|ふ}っ→降る：00839_furu⟧⟦てきた→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ (it has started to rain), ⟦{眠|ねむ}く→眠い：00872_nemui⟧⟦なっ→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦てきた→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧ (I'm getting sleepy).

## Tips for Learners

1. **Let the verb decide what ⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ means.** Ask whether the verb describes an activity (read, run, wait) or an instant change (die, marry, open). Activities give "is doing"; changes give "is in the state of having done."
2. **Learn the contractions as vocabulary.** ⟦てる→てる：30816_teru⟧ (⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧), ⟦とく→とく：30817_toku⟧ (⟦ておく→ておく：30378_teoku⟧), and ⟦ちゃう→ちゃう：08784_chau⟧/じゃう (⟦てしまう→てしまう：03102_teshimau⟧/⟦でしまう→てしまう：03102_teshimau⟧) are the forms you will actually hear.
3. **Watch the particles.** A transitive verb with ⟦てある→てある：30377_tearu⟧ takes ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ on the thing affected: ⟦{鍵|かぎ}→鍵：02189_kagi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧かけ⟦てある→てある：30377_tearu⟧ (the door has been locked).
4. **Keep helpers in kana.** ⟦{持|も}って→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧ may be written with the kanji when the going is literal, but the helper uses in this article are normally written in kana: ⟦なっ→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦ていく→ていく：30814_teiku⟧, ⟦{分|わ}かっ→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧⟦てくる→てくる：30815_tekuru⟧.
5. **Read the entries.** Each helper has its own dictionary entry with more examples; the verbs in the table above carry notes on what ⟦ている→ている：30376_teiru⟧ means for them.
